contributions.statement: Re-measure custom harness components at each model upgrade, because the advantage of a complex harness over a minimal loop shrank by more than half on SWE-style repair as models improved.
contributions.evidence: Table 3 (leaderboard): OpenHands gain +13.60 -> +5.47pp, SWE-agent +9.60 -> +4.07pp from Claude 3.7 to Claude 4 Sonnet; own SWE-bench Pro runs: OpenCode advantage ~6 -> 2.67pp; heterogeneous leaderboard submissions, single runs.

contributions.statement: Do not split an agent into generic SDLC-role subagents (requirements, architecture, coding, testing, repair); they degraded scores, whereas narrow task-specific subagents with restricted tools helped.
contributions.evidence: §5.2.1 component study on ProgramBench, two models, one run each; task-specific subagents tailored to the benchmark and may have gained extra step budget under the 300-step cap (audit).

contributions.statement: LLM-summary compaction can cut prompt tokens 54-77% while lowering task score 4-5 points; treat it as a cost trade-off, not a free win.
contributions.evidence: Table 7 and §5.2.1; one compaction implementation, one task type, single run.

reason: The capability-shrink nuance is useful for deciding how much harness to maintain; component rankings are benchmark-tailored and weak after audit.
